speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. speaker: Doctor
text:
Since the pain is localized to the left knee but the limp suggests a potential proximal issue, has he noticed any pain in his hip or groin, or does the discomfort seem to radiate there?

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal inflammatory markers and the referral pain from the hip to the knee, has he experienced any morning stiffness or reduced range of motion in the left hip joint?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Transient Synovitis of the Left Hip.
